items.entity: Half-MBB design domain (physical length, height and aspect ratio)
items.description: Sec. 3.4 gives only hexagon counts (HNex×HNey = 60×20, 120×40, 300×100). The hexagon size, shape and node coordinates are left to [1] (Sec. 3.1, lines 20–25), and Fig. 1(a) is not available. From 'rfill = 2.4√3 … 0.04 times the maximum length', L = 60√3, so each hexagon is √3 wide. The domain height is never stated. The hexagonal domain also has staggered, zig-zag edges (hanging nodes are removed when HNey is even), so the text does not define which rectangle to use on a structured grid.
readings: Regular hexagons with unit side (width √3, row pitch 1.5): L × H ≈ 60√3 × 30 ≈ 103.9 × 30, aspect ≈ 3.46:1 (≈ 3.41:1 if the outer zig-zag adds 0.5 to H)
Aspect 3:1 (e.g. 60 × 20), treating the hexagon counts like square-element counts as in the 99-line MBB
Hexagon width √3 with unit row height: ≈ 103.9 × 20, aspect ≈ 5.2:1

items.description: Sec. 3.4 lists three meshes (60×20, 120×40, 300×100, with rfill 2.4√3, 4.8√3, 12√3). The Fig. 2 caption assigns the rows to ft values (row 1 = ft=0) but never says which column uses which mesh. The listing order and the falling compliance (C = 298.92 → 293.66 → 282.47) suggest that (a) is 60×20, but this is only implied. The text also says ft=0 designs are mesh-dependent.
readings: 60×20 hexagons (first listed; rfill 2.4√3)
120×40 hexagons (rfill 4.8√3)
300×100 hexagons (rfill 12√3)

items.entity: Structured-grid (quadrilateral) mesh equivalent to the hexagonal mesh
items.description: The paper uses six-node hexagonal elements, each built from two symmetric half-quadrilaterals (Sec. 3.1), with Wachpress shape functions (Sec. 3.2). It gives no element dimensions and no equivalent quadrilateral resolution, so the user must choose the structured grid.
readings: 60×20 square Q4 elements (copy the counts)
≈ 60×17–18 square elements of side √3 (same x-resolution; height of regular hexagons ≈ 30)
≈ 104×30 unit-square elements (element size = hexagon side length)
120×20 rectangular Q4 elements of size (√3/2)×1.5 (the half-quadrilateral sub-grid of the tessellation)

items.entity: Symmetry edge and vertical support of the half-MBB
items.description: Sec. 2 says only that Fig. 1(a) shows 'the symmetric half-design domain … with the pertinent boundary conditions'. Unlike Secs. 4.1–4.2, no fixeddofs listing is given for the MBB beam. So the edge that carries the symmetry condition, and where and over how many nodes the vertical support acts, are shown only in the figure.
readings: u_x = 0 on every node of the left edge (symmetry) and u_y = 0 at the single bottom-right corner node (99-line convention)
Mirrored: u_x = 0 on the right edge and u_y = 0 at the bottom-left corner node
Left-edge symmetry with u_y = 0 on a short run of bottom-edge nodes near the right corner

items.entity: Far-end support at the bottom corner opposite the symmetry edge
items.description: The text does not say whether this support is a roller or a pin; it is shown only in Fig. 1(a). A pin adds horizontal restraint, which gives arch-like behaviour and a different layout.
readings: Roller: only the vertical DOF is fixed (standard MBB)
Pin: both the horizontal and vertical DOFs are fixed

items.description: Sec. 2 refers to the 'external load F' shown in Fig. 1(a). The text gives no position or DOF index for the MBB beam.
readings: Top-left corner node (top of the symmetry edge, i.e. mid-span of the full beam)
Top-right corner node (mirrored set-up with the symmetry condition on the right edge)

items.description: Only Fig. 1(a) shows whether F is a concentrated nodal load or spread over a small patch.
readings: Concentrated load at a single node
Load spread over the 2–3 nodes on the top edge of the corner element

items.description: The text does not give the direction of F; it is shown only in Fig. 1(a). The standard MBB load points downward. Reversing the sign of the single load changes neither the compliance nor the layout.
readings: Vertical, −y (downward)
Vertical, +y (upward)

items.description: The magnitude of F for the MBB beam is not given. The extension listings in Secs. 4.1–4.2 use unit values (data = ±1).
readings: |F| = 0.5 (half of a unit total load on the full beam)

items.description: Sec. 2 gives only the ratio Emin/E0 = 1e-9 and states that k0 is built with E = 1. Sec. 3.2 says E0 and Emin are stored on lines 12–13 but gives no values.
readings: E0 = 1, Emin = 1e-9
Another E0, with Emin = 1e-9·E0

items.description: KE is computed with Wachpress shape functions under plane stress (Sec. 3.2), but ν is never given.
Sec. 3.2 states plane stress but gives no thickness.
readings: Another uniform thickness

items.description: Sec. 3.3 says 'loop, change, maxiter, dv and move are defined on line 80' but gives no values. The only guidance is 'standard optimality criteria [7]' (Sec. 2).
readings: move = 0.2, η = 0.5 (99-line defaults)

items.description: Sec. 3.3 says maxiter is defined on line 80 but gives no value. With no filtering (ft=0), the run may stop at maxiter before it converges.
Sec. 3.3 says convergence and termination are monitored by 'change' and that OcC 'computes the normalized change in x', but gives neither the norm nor the threshold.
readings: max|x_new − x| < 0.01
max|x_new − x| < 0.001

items.entity: Mapping of the ft flag to filter type
items.description: Sec. 3.3 lists 'sensitivity filtering (ft=1), density filtering (ft=1), and null (no) filtering (ft=0)'. The next paragraph says the filtered density is used when ft=2, and the Fig. 2 rows use ft = 0, 1, 2. Fig. 2(a) is ft=0 (no filter) according to the caption, so this conflict matters only if the filtered versions of this MBB example (rows 2–3) are re-run or used as cross-checks.
readings: ft=1 = sensitivity filter, ft=2 = density filter
ft=1 = density filter (literal second label); the flag for the sensitivity filter is then unclear

items.entity: Checkerboard control for the unfiltered (ft=0) design on a structured grid
items.description: Fig. 2(a) is the unfiltered (ft=0) design. The paper relies on edge-connected hexagons to avoid checkerboards (Secs. 1, 3.3, 3.4). It still lists rfill = 2.4√3 for this mesh, although ft=0 does not use it. It gives no guidance for quadrilateral elements, where running with no filter produces checkerboards. The filter weights (HHs, lines 76–77) are also not defined.
readings: No filter at all (literal ft=0; accept checkerboards and point hinges on Q4 elements)
Minimal sensitivity filter with rmin ≈ 1.2–1.5 element widths, used only to suppress checkerboards
Sensitivity filter with rmin = 0.04 × L (rfill = 2.4√3 ≈ 4.16 hexagon-length units ≈ 2.4 hexagon widths) and linear cone weights
